correctness.rationale: PASS: The lateral frustum intrinsic metric dr²+(r sin gamma)² dtheta² develops to an annular Euclidean polar strip with angle period 2phi=2pi sin gamma, where half-period phi<pi. The shortest between radii r,s and shorter developed separation delta<=phi is a straight chord when delta<=acos(b/r)+acos(b/s), otherwise the sum of two tangents and the inner-circle arc. Shorter winding is optimal by contracting angular speed while fixing the radial path. Distance strictly increases with delta>0, and for fixed other endpoint it is a globally convex function of each radius: chord branch has second derivative s² sin²(delta)/distance³, tangent branch has positive b²/(r²sqrt(r²-b²)), with matching first derivatives at contact. Therefore diametral radii lie at corners (B,b) or (B,B); (b,b) is smaller. Comparing their exact values gives mixed-rim chord only if phi<pi/3 and q<2cos phi-1; outer-to-outer chord if otherwise q<=cos(phi/2); and outer rim tangents+inner arc for q>cos(phi/2). The two transition regularities follow by differentiating these branches. Independent 18,225 radial-grid pairs at several rational-angle numerical samples did not violate the derived corner bound. Finite checks corroborate the analytic convexity argument.
